description: Ship Step 9: dev commit blocked by pre-commit hook
remediation: Ship workflow Steps 9/10/Close should commit via a temp branch (`docs/ship-{FID}`) created from dev in a new temp worktree, commit there (branch != dev/main → hook allows), then FF-merge dev from REPO_ROOT. Or: add a hook exception for commit messages matching `[skip ci]`.

description: Post-merge dev CI red: Payload migrate over Supabase IPv6
remediation: Any GitHub-Actions step that opens a _direct_ socket to Supabase Postgres must use the IPv4 **session** pooler (`aws-1-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432`, user `postgres.<ref>`), not the direct host. Transaction pooler (6543) can't run DDL. The Supabase CLI (`db push`) is unaffected — it uses the Management API.

Plan/design step should grep for pre-existing `forbidden-tokens.test.ts` SCAN_DIR + token policies before introducing a new brand/source-type literal into a scanned dir. Part-1 verify (and any verify touching `packages/services/src/corpus` or `packages/ai`) should run the AI-package `forbidden-tokens.test.ts` gate, not only typecheck + co-located unit tests.

description: Branch push blocked: lint-staged prettier --write disagrees with pre-push prettier --check
remediation: Plan/design/build close + summary steps that push a branch should run `pnpm format:check` (or a `prettier --write` over `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/`) BEFORE `git push`, not rely on per-commit lint-staged. Alternatively make lint-staged + format:check share one resolved prettier invocation so `--write` is guaranteed to satisfy `--check`.

description: Build plan-1 spike blocked — opencode not installed
Build WS-7 mirror render — `pnpm bkit install` silently flips opencodeProvider + `--opencode` scopes install
remediation: WS-7 mirror re-render in bkit-repo builds must pin the provider AND select all hosts: `pnpm bkit install --claude --cursor --opencode=<committed bkit.opencodeProvider>`. Better: make install preserve an existing `package.json` `bkit.opencodeProvider` (read-existing-then-default) so a plain dogfood install is idempotent on the provider.

description: bkit-design.md Step 10.4 STRAY guard allowlists only `docs/plans/` + `.bkit/friction.md`, but the design phase legitimately appends sanctioned deferral rows to `docs/deferrals.jsonl` (per rules.md Never-drop) and friction to `.bkit/friction.jsonl`; the squash-merge to dev therefore trips the guard on `docs/deferrals.jsonl`, and the allowlist references a stale `.bkit/friction.md` (wrong extension).

Step 3.1 mcp__github__search_issues returns total_count:0 for every query against cbartens/bkit, including the control probe `repo:cbartens/bkit bkit`. Not a genuine zero-hit result — the GitHub issue-search index is unavailable for this repo under the current token (private repo + fine-grained PAT; same class as the known GH_TOKEN project/admin scope gap). Related-issues context is therefore lost for every design/plan/build run in this repo, silently: the workflow maps 0 hits to `None.`, which reads as `nothing related exists` rather than `search did not work`.
remediation: Durable fix: have the related-issues step run a control probe (a query that MUST match, e.g. `repo:{OWNER_REPO} is:issue`) and, when the probe returns 0, write `Search unavailable.` instead of `None.` — 0-hits and index-unavailable must not collapse to the same artifact text. Consider an `env -u GH_TOKEN` keyring-token fallback (same pattern as the Projects v2 403 workaround) or fall back to mcp__github__list_issues, which is not index-backed.

description: Orchestrator fixed a malformed docs/decisions.jsonl row with `head -n -1 file > new` — a GNU-coreutils-only idiom. On macOS/BSD `head` this errors `illegal line count -- -1` and writes NOTHING, but the shell has already truncated the redirect target, and the subsequent `>> ` append leaves a file containing ONLY the last row. Result: docs/decisions.jsonl went 34 rows -> 1, silently destroying 33 append-only decision records. The `&& echo identical` diff guard gave a FALSE all-clear because both sides of the diff were produced by the same failing `head` (empty == empty). Platform is darwin (stated in the environment), so this is a live hazard for any workflow/agent bash that assumes GNU flags.
remediation: Never use `head -n -1` in bkit workflow/agent bash — use BSD-safe `sed ` (or `awk NR>1` for head-trimming). Two structural lessons: (1) prefer append-only edits over read-modify-rewrite on the *.jsonl ledgers; a rewrite makes total loss one bad flag away. (2) A verification diff MUST NOT be built from the same command being verified — compare against `git show HEAD:path`, which is what actually caught this. Consider a shipped rule under rules.md / testing.md: `ledger rewrites must diff --numstat against HEAD and assert 0 deletions`.

description: Two of eight plan subagents failed their artifact contract in the same session, each needing an orchestrator round-trip to fix. (1) @bkit-plan-complexity-check returned its FULL analysis as chat output and never called Write — `plan-complexity-check.md` did not exist (tool_uses=2: it read the plan and replied). (2) @bkit-plan-update stopped mid-item leaving `Verdict: PENDING` in `plan-v2-reviewed.md`. The workflow prescribes Failure Path for a missing artifact, which is far too heavy when the agent HAS the content and merely did not persist it — and the orchestrator is PROHIBITED from writing the artifact itself (`Inlining subagent steps or producing output directly is NOT compliance`), so the only compliant remedy is a re-invoke.
remediation: Give the missing-artifact case the same in-contract remedy the invalid-verdict case already has (`invoke offending subagent again with ...; if still invalid -> Failure Path`) instead of routing straight to Failure Path — a re-invoke to persist already-computed output is cheap and preserves the subagent-authors-the-artifact invariant. Structural fix worth considering: subagent prompts should state that the FILE is the deliverable and the chat return is only a receipt. Also: the orchestrator should assert artifact existence BEFORE the status/commit call, not in the same `&&` chain — here the premature commit recorded a step-done whose `artifacts` entry did not exist on disk.

description: bkit-design Step 3.1 related-issues search via mcp__github__search_issues returned 0 hits for every query on this PRIVATE repo (control query `repo:cbartens/bkit is:issue is:open` -> 0, while gh api search/issues -> 39). Any consumer with a private repo silently gets `None.` for related issues on every design run.
remediation: Step 3.1 should not accept 0 hits at face value: either run a cheap control probe to distinguish `search broken` from `no hits`, or route through the #341 6b/6c mapped gh fallback. Also widen 6i: `trackers stay on MCP` currently has no guard for MCP returning a silently-wrong empty result.

description: MCP related-issues search returns 0 hits for EVERY query on this PRIVATE repo, in both bkit-design Step 3.1 and bkit-plan Step 3.1 — the step is shared, so the defect is workflow-independent. Confirmed again on #58 (plan) 2026-07-15: probes `counter attempt status.jsonl workflow in:title,body` -> 0, `counter attempt in:title,body` -> 0, `repo:cbartens/bkit counter-bus` -> 0, and CONTROL `repo:cbartens/bkit telemetry` -> 0 despite #234 being a telemetry issue whose body is dense with the word. A 0 from mcp__github__search_issues on a private repo is indistinguishable from a genuine no-hits result, and both workflows' step contracts map 0 hits to writing `None.` — so the artifact asserts there are no related issues when the search never ran.
remediation: Both bkit-design and bkit-plan Step 3.1 must not accept 0 hits at face value: run a cheap control probe (a term certain to match) to distinguish `search broken` from `no hits`, and write `Search unavailable.` on a failed control. Fix belongs in the shared step contract, not per-workflow. Alternative: route through the #341 6b/6c mapped gh fallback once it exists. Also widen 6i — `trackers stay on MCP` has no guard for MCP returning a silently-wrong empty result.

description: Plan subagents fail their artifact contract by stopping before the verdict header, recurring across sessions and across agents. Confirmed again on #58 (plan) 2026-07-15: @bkit-plan-update wrote a COMPLETE 677-line plan-v2-reviewed.md (body finished through its verification section) but left line 1 as `Verdict: PENDING`, and returned a mid-task progress narration (`Now the docs table and Automated Tests, then structural verification`) instead of a receipt. The file is 125KB of finished work gated on one unwritten line. Prior occurrences: @bkit-plan-complexity-check returned its full analysis as chat and never called Write; @bkit-plan-update stopped mid-item leaving Verdict: PENDING. The common shape is the agent treating its chat reply as the deliverable and the file as a side effect, and the verdict header — written FIRST, known LAST — is the field most exposed to it.
remediation: Two structural fixes. (1) Subagent prompts must state that the FILE is the deliverable and the chat return is only a receipt — this session's orchestrator said exactly that in every invoke and the failure still recurred, so prompt wording alone is NOT sufficient; the verdict header being written first but only knowable last is the actual trap. Consider requiring the verdict be APPENDED at the end (or written in a final dedicated step) rather than pre-seeded as PENDING at the top. (2) Step 5.3's re-invoke remedy says `Re-emit ONLY the verdict, do NOT redo work` — that is wrong when the agent stopped with real work outstanding, since a verdict-only re-emit would certify incomplete work. The remedy should distinguish `finished but unlabelled` from `stopped mid-item`. Give the missing-artifact case the same in-contract re-invoke remedy the invalid-verdict case has, instead of routing to Failure Path.

summary: API error mid-subagent leaves a valid-looking artifact that passes every gate
description: @bkit-plan-update was terminated by `API Error: Connection closed mid-response` during plan-apply-scope on #58. The harness surfaced the partial output and flagged it incomplete, but the artifact on disk (plan-v3-checked.md, 736 lines) had ALREADY been written with a VALID `Verdict: CONCERNS` header, zero PENDING markers, and a complete-looking tail — so it satisfied every assertion the workflow step prescribes (exists, non-empty, valid verdict, no PENDING). The agent's cut-off sentence (`Now wiring T5.4 into the gates and verification plan`) was the only signal that work remained. It was real: T5.4 was wired into the matrix, tasks and Gate 2, but NOT into the Verification Plan, which still read `Both new rules demonstrably fire: T5.1 and T5.3` and exercised only T5.3 at Step 4c. A rule that never fires is not evidence, so the gap would have shipped the plan's own residual-risk closure unexercised.
remediation: The verdict header is NOT a completion signal — an agent can write a valid verdict and still be mid-task, so the step gates (exists / non-empty / valid verdict / no PENDING) cannot distinguish finished from interrupted. When a subagent returns a partial-output / API-error marker, the orchestrator must verify the artifact INTERNALLY (cross-check the agent's own claimed counts, and trace every newly-introduced task/symbol through to every section that must reference it) rather than re-reading the header. Cheapest durable fix: subagents emit the verdict as their LAST write AND state claimed counts in the receipt, so orchestrator verification is a diff against a claim rather than an open-ended read. A plan-internal consistency check is mechanical and would have caught this: task count == Done-when count, and every task ID in the matrix appears in both the runbook and the verification plan.
